        sheet = "OS count") %>%

```{r Rotifer Data Tidying, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
#Combine Offshore (OS) and Nearshore (NS) count datasets
Erie_2024_Full_Data <- full_join(Erie_2024_D20_Counts, Erie_2024_Nearshore_Counts, copy = F)

# Combine Offshore (OS) and Nearshore (NS) sample metadata 
Erie_2024_Meta_Join <- full_join(Erie_2024_D20_Sample, Erie_2024_Nearshore_Sample, copy = F)

# Combine Offshore (OS) and Nearshore (NS) count and metadata sets together
Erie_2024_Joined <- Erie_2024_Full_Data %>%
  left_join(select(Erie_2024_Meta_Join, "Sample ID", "Basin", "Season", "D or N", "Site Depth", "Lat", "Lon"), by = "Sample ID")

write_csv(Erie_2024_Joined, file = "C:/Users/cmars/OneDrive/Desktop/CCM Work Files/Rotifer Projects/Nearshore-Rotifers/Erie/Processed Data/Erie_2024_Joined.csv")

#Summarise count data and complete with implicit zeros for each Speccode; fill group and type columns with appropriate metadata
Erie_2024_Complete <- Erie_2024_Joined %>%
    group_by(Speccode, Station, Group, Type, Basin, Season, `D or N`, `Site Depth`, Lat, Lon) %>%
    summarise(Zoop_Bio_Sum_m3 = sum(`Biomass mg.m3`), Zoop_Den_Sum_m3 = sum(`Density m3`), Zoop_Bio_Sum_m2 = sum(`Areal Bio mg.m2`)) %>%
    ungroup %>%
    complete(Speccode, nesting(Station, Season), fill = list(Zoop_Bio_Sum_m3 = 0, Zoop_Den_Sum_m3 = 0, Zoop_Bio_Sum_m2 = 0)) %>%
    group_by(Speccode) %>%
    fill(Group, .direction = "downup") %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    group_by(Station) %>%
    fill(Type, Basin, Season, `D or N`, `Site Depth`, Lat, Lon, .direction = "downup") %>%
    ungroup()
```

```{r Rotifer Genera For Loop, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# For Loop setup for Rotifer Genera column
Speccode <- Erie_2024_Complete$Speccode
GENUS_Length <- length(Speccode)
Rot_GENERA <- rep("NA", GENUS_Length)
  for(x in 1:GENUS_Length){
      if (Speccode[x] == "ASCOVAL" || Speccode[x] == "ASCECAU") {
      Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Ascomorpha"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "ASPHERR" || Speccode[x] == "ASPPRIO" || Speccode[x] == "ASPBRIG") {
        Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Asplanchna"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "BRACALC" || Speccode[x] == "BRAANGU" || Speccode[x] == "BRABUDA" || Speccode[x] == "BRADIVE" || Speccode[x] == "BRAHAVA" || Speccode[x] == "BRARUBE" || Speccode[x] == "BRASP" || Speccode[x] == "BRAURCE" || Speccode[x] == "BRAVARI") {
          Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Brachionus"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "CEPSP") {
          Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Cephalodella"     
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "COLSP" || Speccode[x] == "COLMUTA" || Speccode[x] == "CONNATA") {
          Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Collotheca"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "COUSP") {
          Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Colurella"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "COOUNIC") {
            Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Conochilus"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "CONSP") {
            Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Conochiloides"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "ENCSP") {
              Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Encentrum"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "EUCMENE" || Speccode[x] == "EUCSP") {
              Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Euchlanis"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "FILLONG" || Speccode[x] == "FILTERM") {
              Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Filinia"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "GASSTYL") {
              Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Gastropus"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "KELLONG") {
                Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Kellicottia"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "KERCOCH" || Speccode[x] == "KEREARL" || Speccode[x] == "KERCRAS" || Speccode[x] == "KERCOCHH" || Speccode[x] == "KERQUAD" || Speccode[x] == "KERHIEM" || Speccode[x] == "KERSP" || Speccode[x] == "KERCOCHT" || Speccode[x] == "KERTEST" || Speccode[x] == "KERVALGT") {
                  Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Keratella"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "LECFLEX" || Speccode[x] == "LECSP") {
                  Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Lecane"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "LEPSP") {
                  Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Lepadella"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "MONCOPE" || Speccode[x] == "MONSP") {
                  Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Monostyla"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "MYTSP") {
                  Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Mytilina"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "NOOSP") {
                  Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Notomatta" 
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "NOTACUM" || Speccode[x] == "NOTLABI" || Speccode[x] == "NOTLAUR" || Speccode[x] == "NOTSP" || Speccode[x] == "NOTSQUA" || Speccode[x] == "NOTFOLI") {
                  Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Notholca"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "PLOHUDS" || Speccode[x] == "PLOTRUN" || Speccode[x] == "PLOLENT") {
                    Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Ploesoma"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "POLREMA" || Speccode[x] == "POLVULG" || Speccode[x] == "POLSP" || Speccode[x] == "POLDOLI" || Speccode[x] == "POLMAJO") {
                      Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Polyarthra"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "POMSULC") {
                     Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Pompholyx"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "PROSP") {
                     Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Proales"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "TRIMULT" || Speccode[x] == "TRIPUSI" || Speccode[x] == "TRISP" || Speccode[x] == "TRICYLI" || Speccode[x] == "TRICAPU" || Speccode[x] == "TRIELON" || Speccode[x] == "TRISIMI") {
                        Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Trichocerca"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "TYLMONO") {
                          Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Tylotrocha"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "TRCPOCI") {
                          Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Trichotria"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "SYNSP") {
                          Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Synchaeta"
        } else if (Speccode[x] == "ROTBDEL") {
                            Rot_GENERA[x] <- "Rotifer Bdelloid"}
  }

# Binding the Rot_GENERA variable created with for loop as a column to the original dataframe
Erie_2024_Complete <- cbind(Erie_2024_Complete, Rot_GENERA)

# For Loop setup for Zoop Taxa column
Group <- Erie_2024_Complete$Group
Group_Length <- length(Group)
Zoop_Taxa <- rep("NA", Group_Length)
  for(x in 1:Group_Length){
      if (Group[x] == "NDAP") {
          Zoop_Taxa[x] <- "Non-Daphnid"
        } else if (Group[x] == "ROT") {
          Zoop_Taxa[x] <- "Rotifers"
        } else if (Group[x] == "NAU") {
          Zoop_Taxa[x] <- "Nauplii"     
        } else if (Group[x] == "DVEL") {
          Zoop_Taxa[x] <- "Veligers"
        } else if (Group[x] == "CAL") {
          Zoop_Taxa[x] <- "Calanoids"
        } else if (Group[x] == "CYC") {
          Zoop_Taxa[x] <- "Cyclopoids"
        } else if (Group[x] == "DAP") {
          Zoop_Taxa[x] <- "Daphnids"
        } else if (Group[x] == "PRED") {
          Zoop_Taxa[x] <- "Predatory Cladocerans"
        } else if (Group[x] == "MAL") {
          Zoop_Taxa[x] <- "Mysids"}
  }

# Binding the Zoop_Taxa variable created with for loop as a column to the original dataframe
Erie_2024_Complete <- cbind(Erie_2024_Complete, Zoop_Taxa)

write_csv(Erie_2024_Complete, file = "C:/Users/cmars/OneDrive/Desktop/CCM Work Files/Rotifer Projects/Nearshore-Rotifers/Erie/Processed Data/Erie_2024_Complete.csv")

# Summarize all zoop and rotifer volumetric data by SPECCODE,

    #filter(CRUISE_DECODE == "Spring") %>%
    filter(str_starts(Station, "ER")) %>%
    group_by(Speccode, Zoop_Taxa, Type, Season) %>%
      summarise(All_Bio_SUM_m3 = sum(Zoop_Bio_Sum_m3),
      All_Den_SUM_m3 = sum(Zoop_Den_Sum_m3),
      All_Bio_SUM_m2 = sum(Zoop_Bio_Sum_m2),
      All_Bio_MEAN_m3 = mean(Zoop_Bio_Sum_m3),
      All_Den_MEAN_m3 = mean(Zoop_Den_Sum_m3),

```{r ANOVA and Linear Model Statistics, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}

#Fit the Linear Mixed Model with lmer()
Rotifer_Bio_Station <- Erie_2024_Complete %>% 
  filter(Group == "ROT") %>%
  filter(str_starts(Station, "ER")) %>%
  group_by(Station, Rot_GENERA, Type, Season) %>%
    summarise(All_Bio_SUM_m3 = sum(Zoop_Bio_Sum_m3),
    All_Den_SUM_m3 = sum(Zoop_Den_Sum_m3)) 

#Fit the Linear Mixed Model with lmer()
Zoop_Bio_Station <- Erie_2024_Complete %>% 
  filter(str_starts(Station, "ER")) %>%
  group_by(Station, Zoop_Taxa, Type, Season) %>%
    summarise(All_Bio_SUM_m3 = sum(Zoop_Bio_Sum_m3),
    All_Den_SUM_m3 = sum(Zoop_Den_Sum_m3)) 

#Identify data outliers for biomass and density
Complete_Rotifer_Outliers <- Rotifer_Bio_Station %>%
  group_by(Rot_GENERA, Type, Season) %>%
  mutate(
    #Density outlier detection
    Q1_Density = quantile(All_Den_SUM_m3, 0.25),
    Q3_Density = quantile(All_Den_SUM_m3, 0.75),
    IQR_Density = Q3_Density - Q1_Density,
    is_outlier_Density = All_Den_SUM_m3 < (Q1_Density - 3 * IQR_Density) | All_Den_SUM_m3 > (Q3_Density + 3 * IQR_Density),
    #Biomass outlier detection
    Q1_Biomass = quantile(All_Bio_SUM_m3, 0.25),
    Q3_Biomass = quantile(All_Bio_SUM_m3, 0.75),
    IQR_Biomass = Q3_Biomass - Q1_Biomass,
    is_outlier_Biomass = All_Bio_SUM_m3 < (Q1_Biomass - 3 * IQR_Biomass) | All_Bio_SUM_m3 > (Q3_Biomass + 3 * IQR_Biomass),
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

#Identify data outliers for biomass and density
Complete_Zoop_Outliers <- Zoop_Bio_Station %>%
  group_by(Zoop_Taxa, Type, Season) %>%
  mutate(
    #Density outlier detection
    Q1_Density = quantile(All_Den_SUM_m3, 0.25),
    Q3_Density = quantile(All_Den_SUM_m3, 0.75),
    IQR_Density = Q3_Density - Q1_Density,
    is_outlier_Density = All_Den_SUM_m3 < (Q1_Density - 3 * IQR_Density) | All_Den_SUM_m3 > (Q3_Density + 3 * IQR_Density),
    #Biomass outlier detection
    Q1_Biomass = quantile(All_Bio_SUM_m3, 0.25),
    Q3_Biomass = quantile(All_Bio_SUM_m3, 0.75),
    IQR_Biomass = Q3_Biomass - Q1_Biomass,
    is_outlier_Biomass = All_Bio_SUM_m3 < (Q1_Biomass - 3 * IQR_Biomass) | All_Bio_SUM_m3 > (Q3_Biomass + 3 * IQR_Biomass),
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

#Remove outliers prior to visualizations and statistical analyses ***** May be removing too much resolution - taken out to check model fit with only 28 true biomass and density outliers 
#Complete_Rotifer_Outliers <- Complete_Rotifer_Outliers %>%
 # filter(!is_outlier_Density & !is_outlier_Biomass) %>%
  #select(-starts_with("Q1"), -starts_with("Q3"), -starts_with("IQR"), -is_outlier_Density, -is_outlier_Biomass)

#Filter biomass models by season prior to anova and lmer statistics
Rotifer_Bio_Summer_model <- Complete_Rotifer_Outliers %>% 
  filter(Season == "Summer") %>% 
  filter(!Rot_GENERA %in% c("Cephalodella", "Colurella", "Encentrum", "Lecane", "Monostyla", "Notholca", "Notomatta", "Rotifer Bdelloid", "Tylotrocha"))

Rotifer_Bio_Spring_model <- Complete_Rotifer_Outliers %>% 
  filter(Season == "Spring") %>% 
  filter(!Rot_GENERA %in% c("Ascomorpha", "Asplanchna", "Gastropus", "Ploesoma", "Tylotrocha"))

#Filter biomass models by season prior to anova and lmer statistics
Zoop_Bio_Summer_model <- Complete_Zoop_Outliers %>% 
  filter(Season == "Summer") %>% 
  filter(!Zoop_Taxa %in% c("Mysids"))

#Filter biomass models by season prior to anova and lmer statistics
Zoop_Bio_Spring_model <- Complete_Zoop_Outliers %>% 
  filter(Season == "Spring") %>% 
  filter(!Zoop_Taxa %in% c("Predatory Cladocerans"))

# summer model - rank transformation makes the data more normalized compared to decostand hellinger transformation
Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Summer <- aov(rank(All_Bio_SUM_m3) ~ Type + Rot_GENERA,
  data = Rotifer_Bio_Summer_model,
  contrasts = list(
    Type = "contr.sum",
    Rot_GENERA = "contr.sum"
  )
)

Anova(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Summer, type = "3")
plot(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Summer, which = 2)
hist(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Summer$residuals)
plot(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Summer, which = 3)
ggqqplot(resid(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Summer))

shapiro_test(resid(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Summer))
moments::skewness(resid(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Summer))
tapply(Rotifer_Bio_Summer_model$All_Bio_SUM_m3, Rotifer_Bio_Summer_model$Type, FUN = var)

Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Summer <- emmeans(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Summer, pairwise ~ Type + Rot_GENERA)
Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Summer_regridded <- regrid(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Summer, transform = "response")
contrast(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Summer_regridded, method = "pairwise")

Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Summer_Category <- emmeans(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Summer, ~ Type + Rot_GENERA)
print(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Summer_Category)

Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Summer_Category %>% 
  pairs() %>% 
  test(joint = TRUE)
pairs(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Summer_Category)

# spring model - rank transformation makes the data more normalized compred to decostand hellinger transformation
Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Spring <- aov(rank(All_Bio_SUM_m3) ~ Type + Rot_GENERA,
  data = Rotifer_Bio_Spring_model,
  contrasts = list(
    Type = "contr.sum",
    Rot_GENERA = "contr.sum"
  )
)

Anova(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Spring, type = "3")
plot(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Spring, which = 2)
hist(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Spring$residuals)
plot(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Spring, which = 3)
ggqqplot(resid(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Spring))

shapiro_test(resid(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Spring))
moments::skewness(resid(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Spring))
tapply(Rotifer_Bio_Spring_model$All_Bio_SUM_m3, Rotifer_Bio_Spring_model$Type, FUN = var)

Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Spring <- emmeans(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Spring, pairwise ~ Type + Rot_GENERA)
Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Spring_regridded <- regrid(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Spring, transform = "response")
contrast(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Spring_regridded, method = "pairwise")

Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Spring_Category <- emmeans(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_Spring, ~ Type + Rot_GENERA)
print(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Spring_Category)

Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Spring_Category %>% 
  pairs() %>% 
  test(joint = TRUE)
pairs(Rotifer_Bio_ANOVA_EMM_Spring_Category)

### Summer LME Model
# Fit summer linear mixed effect model; Use these p values and results - Collotheca only significant
Rotifer_Bio_LMM_Summer <- lmer(
  rank(All_Bio_SUM_m3) ~ Rot_GENERA * Type +     # Fixed effects: Rot_GENERA, Type
  (1 | Station),                                    # Random effects: Stations
  data = Rotifer_Bio_Summer_model, REML = TRUE,
)

summary(Rotifer_Bio_LMM_Summer)
anova(Rotifer_Bio_LMM_Summer, type = 3)

# Compute estimated marginal means
Rotifer_Bio_Summer_emmeans <- emmeans(Rotifer_Bio_LMM_Summer, ~ Type | Rot_GENERA)  # Compare genera among type 

#Games-Howell Post-Hoc Test for unequal variances and sample sizes

# Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons
Rotifer_Bio_Summer_tukey <- contrast(Rotifer_Bio_Summer_emmeans, method = "pairwise", adjust = "tukey")

# View results
summary(Rotifer_Bio_Summer_tukey)

kable(Rotifer_Bio_Summer_tukey)

Figure 1A shows the volumetric biomass of the 13 most commonly
encountered taxa between the nearshore and offshore samples for Lake Erie in
August 2024. With several exceptions, most rotifer taxa exhibited higher
average biomass values in the offshore samples, suggesting that these
waters supported higher densities and perhaps larger taxa compared to
shallower habitats. Several exceptions to this were *Trichocerca*, which had
a higher biomass in the nearshore vs. offshore, and can be attributed to
the higher nutrient concentrations found in nearshore waters supporting
a greater density of these eutrophic-loving taxa (Gannon and Stemberger
1978; Sládecek, 1983). *Synchaeta* and *Ploesoma* showed a 
slight preference for the nearshore waters while *Conochiloides* showed a 
preference for the offshore waters. The remaining taxa *Polyarthra*, 
*Ascomorpha*, *Brachionus*, *Keratella*, etc, exhibited very similar biomass 
values between near- and offshore waters. These insights suggest that despite 
potentially higher food concentrations in nearshore habitats, only several taxa 
gain a clear advantage in these conditions.

```{r Summer NS-OS Rotifer Genera Average Density Barplot, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Figure 1B. Summer Rotifer genera nearshore (NS) vs. offshore (OS) average density (# per m^3^). Error bars represent standard errors of the means. Taxa groups are identified in legend by color.", fig.height=8, fig.width=12, message=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

# Rotifer Genera Summary Stats Summer Filter
Rot_Genera_Sum_Stats_Summer <- Rot_Genera_Sum_Stats %>%  
  filter(Season == "Summer") %>% 
  filter(Rot_GENERA != "Pompholyx" & Rot_GENERA != "Rotifer Bdelloid" & Rot_GENERA != "Trichotria" & Rot_GENERA != "Lepadella" & Rot_GENERA != "Monostyla" & Rot_GENERA != "Filinia") %>%
  filter(All_Bio_SUM_m3 > 0)

#!Rot_GENERA %in% c

# Ordering of Rot_GENERA column
Rot_Genera_Sum_Stats_Summer$Rot_GENERA <- factor(Rot_Genera_Sum_Stats_Summer$Rot_GENERA, levels = c("Trichocerca", "Polyarthra", "Synchaeta", "Ascomorpha", "Conochilus", "Brachionus", "Keratella", "Kellicottia", "Ploesoma", "Collotheca", "Gastropus", "Conochiloides", "Asplanchna"))

# creating a color palette for rotifer genera stack graph
cb_Rot_GENERA_Palette <- c("green2", "yellow2", "red2", "navy", "saddlebrown", "blue1", "magenta3", "cyan3", "orange3", "mediumaquamarine", "seagreen4", "gray34", "gray60")

# Stacked bar plots of mean biomass of Nearshore and Offshore rotifer Rot_GENERA
gg_NS_OF_DEN_Rot_Genera_Summer <- ggplot(Rot_Genera_Sum_Stats_Summer, aes(x = Type, y = All_Den_MEAN_m3, fill = Rot_GENERA)) +
    geom_bar(color = "black", stat = "identity") +
    facet_grid(~Rot_GENERA, scales = "free") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymax = All_Den_MEAN_m3 + All_Den_SE_m3, ymin = All_Den_MEAN_m3 - All_Den_SE_m3), width = .8) +
#geom_bar_pattern(aes(pattern_angle = SUMGROUP, pattern_spacing = SUMGROUP), stat = "identity", color = "black", pattern_colour = "darkgray", pattern_fill = "darkgray", fill = "white") +
#panel border, axis text and title sizes and orientations
    theme_cowplot() +
      theme(panel.border = element_rect(linetype = "solid"), strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", angle = 45, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1), axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 24, face = "bold"), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 24, face = "bold"), plot.title = element_blank(), plot.background = element_rect(fill = 'white', color = NA)) +
#legend details
      theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.42,0.85), legend.box.background = element_rect(), legend.box.margin = margin(3,3,3,3), legend.text = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold")) +
      guides(fill=guide_legend(nrow = 7)) +
#scale_pattern_manual(values = c(SUMG_WWC_Pattern)) +
#palette color for bar fills; see Barbiero for reference
      scale_fill_manual(values = c(cb_Rot_GENERA_Palette)) +
      labs(x = "NS-OS", y = bquote("Density"~("#"/m^3)))

gg_NS_OF_DEN_Rot_Genera_Summer
```

Figure 1B shows the density of the 13 most commonly encountered 
taxa between the nearshore and offshore samples for Lake Erie in
August 2024. With several exceptions, most rotifer taxa exhibited higher
average density values in the nearshore samples, which is in contrast to 
average biomass values, indicating that smaller specimens or species are found 
in shallower habitats. Several taxa (*Trichocerca*, *Polyarthra*, *Synchaeta*, 
*Ascomorpha*) showed higher densities in the nearshore vs. offshore waters. 
*Conochiloides* was the only taxa that showed a clear preference for the 
offshore waters. The remaining taxa *Brachionus*, *Keratella*, *Kellicottia*, 
etc, exhibited very similar density values between near- and offshore waters. 
These insights suggest that despite potentially higher food concentrations in 
nearshore habitats, only several taxa gain an advantage in these conditions. 
Additionally, the contrasting findings that densities for several taxa are 
higher in the nearshore while biomass is similar or higher in the offshore, 
indicates there is a different rotifer community between the sample types.

## Lake Erie 2024 Study Area Station Map

```{r OS-NS 2024 Rotifer Stations, fig.cap="Figure 4. Rotifer study area for 2024 samples collected at the 20 offshore sites (OS - blue filled circles), and the 12 CSMI nearshore sites (NS - black filled boxes).", fig.height=6, fig.width=12}
#Study Area figure 1 for report - Erie OS-NS stations
devtools::install_github("ropensci/rnaturalearthhires")

us_states <- ne_states(country = "United States of America", returnclass = "sf")
canada_provinces <- ne_states(country = "Canada", returnclass = "sf")

lakes <- ne_download(scale = 10, type = "lakes", category = "physical", returnclass = "sf")

# Ordering of Rot_GENERA column
Rotifer_Full_Stations$Type <- factor(Rotifer_Full_Stations$Type, levels = c("OS", "NS"))

great_lakes_names <- c("Lake Superior", "Lake Michigan", "Lake Huron", "Lake Erie", "Lake Ontario")
great_lakes <- lakes[lakes$name %in% great_lakes_names, ]

Erie_Rotifer_Station_Map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = us_states, fill = "gray", color = "black", size = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = canada_provinces, fill = "gray", color = "black", size = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = great_lakes, fill = "white", color = "black", size = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = Rotifer_Full_Stations, size=4, stroke=1, colour = "black", aes(x = Lon, y = Lat, group = Type, fill = Type, shape = Type)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("OS" = "#1b98e0", "NS" = "#353436")) +
  geom_text(data = Rotifer_Full_Stations, aes(x = Lon, y = Lat, label = sub("^ER", "", Station)),
            size = 4,
            fontface = "bold",
            vjust = -1,    # Shifts text vertically above the point
            hjust = 0.5,   # Centers text horizontally
            check_overlap = TRUE) + # Keeps map clean by hiding overlapping text
  theme_cowplot() +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(linetype = "solid", fill = NA), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20), plot.title = element_text(size = 26, hjust = 0.5)) +
  theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 20), legend.position = "right", legend.box.background = element_rect(), legend.box.margin = margin(3,3,3,3), legend.text = element_text(size = 20)) +
  labs(title = "Lake Erie 2024 Stations") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-83.5, -79.0), ylim = c(41.4, 42.9))

Erie_Rotifer_Station_Map
```

    theme_cowplot() +

```

Figure 5A represents the individual station total rotifer biomass for the 13 
most common taxa collected during the Lake Erie August 2024 survey. The stations 
are separated by the nearshore (NS) and offshore (OS) samples ordered from east 
to west. The first 7 listed nearshore samples were collected from the northshore 
of Lake Erie and show a lower overall biomass compared with the 5 subsequent 
stations collected from the southshore of the lake. That biomass disparity is 
largely driven by higher *Asplanchna* values in several southshore samples. 
Station ER936n shows a particularly diverse community compared with other 
stations, and is close in proximity to Van Buren Bay close to Dunkirk, NY. The 
offshore samples are separated by their basins (4 east, 10 central, 6 west), 
which are distinct due to the large change in bathymetric depths between basins,
resulting in very different ecological implications for the zooplankton 
communities. The eastern basin is the deepest and most similar to the Lake 
Ontario rotifer community, and with the exception of ER15M which is missing the 
large *Asplanchna* biomass, those 4 samples are similar. The first 3 central 
samples are similar with relatively low overall biomass with the addition of 
more *Polyarthra*. With the exception of ER42 which shows a massive *Asplancha* 
biomass, the remaining central stations exhibit a similar community, with more 
*Polyarthra* and *Trichocera* biomass moving westward. The western basin is 
historically the most diverse community in the Great Lakes, with very shallow 
and eutrophic waters that support a unique assemblage of rotifers. A higher 
proportion of *Trichocera*, *Polyarthra*, and *Brachionus* is indication of 
greater nutrient availability, and therefore a more diverse set of food 
resources compared with other localities. It should be noted that the despite 
these resources, the western basin often exhibits the lowest biomass and density 
of rotifers, which is impacted by the shallow waters (~6 meters), discharge from
the Detroit River and Maumee River, and higher potential of predation by 
larger zooplankton and larval fish.

      theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.30,0.90), legend.box.background = element_rect(), legend.box.margin = margin(3,3,3,3), legend.text = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold")) +
      guides(fill=guide_legend(nrow = 4)) +
#scale_pattern_manual(values = c(SUMG_WWC_Pattern)) +
#palette color for bar fills; see Barbiero for reference
      scale_fill_manual(values = c(Barb_Palette)) + 
      labs(x = "NS-OS", y = bquote("Volumetric Biomass"~(mg/m^3))) 
      
gg_NS_OS_BIO_Zoop_Stations_Summer
```

# Ordering of Zoop Taxa column

# Structure for Barbiero similar color palette
Barb_Palette <- c("darkgreen", "orange2", "slategray3", "blue2", "yellow2", "red2", "purple3", "chocolate4")

# Ordering of Rot_GENERA column
Zoop_Bio_Spring_model$Station <- factor(Zoop_Bio_Spring_model$Station, levels = c("ER09", "ER10", "ER15M", "ER63", "ER30", "ER31", "ER32", "ER78M", "ER36", "ER37", "ER38", "ER73", "ER42", "ER43", "ER91M", "ER92", "ER58", "ER59", "ER60", "ER61", "ER932n", "ER937n", "ERN22n", "ER951n", "ER959n", "ERG09n", "ER966n", "ER936n", "ERI28n",  "ER95b", "ER958n", "ER964n"))

# Ordering of Rot_GENERA column

# Stacked bar plots of total biomass for Nearshore and Offshore stations rotifer genera

#panel border, axis text and title sizes and orientations

      theme(panel.border = element_rect(linetype = "solid"), strip.text = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1), axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 24, face = "bold"), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 24, face = "bold"), plot.title = element_blank(), plot.background = element_rect(fill = 'white', color = NA)) +
      #legend details
      theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.20,0.9), legend.box.background = element_rect(), legend.box.margin = margin(3,3,3,3), legend.text = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold")) +

      scale_fill_manual(values = c(Barb_Palette)) +
